title: Why Would God Allow Scripture to Be Corrupted?
subtitle: Human responsibility, earlier scripture, and the Quran's promise of preservation
summary: Islam does not teach that God abandoned humanity when earlier scripture was altered or misread. Communities were entrusted with revelation, but some concealed or distorted it. Later prophets corrected people, and the Quran came as the final criterion with a distinct promise of preservation.

seo.metaTitle: Why Would God Allow Scripture to Be Corrupted?
seo.metaDescription: Why Islam says earlier scripture could be distorted, how tahrif is understood, and why the Quran carries a distinct preservation promise.

sections.title: The Question in Brief
sections.body:
If God revealed the Torah and Gospel, why allow people to mishandle them? The Islamic answer begins with human responsibility. God gives guidance, but people can obey, neglect, hide, or misrepresent it. He continued to send prophets, and the Quran came as the final protected criterion.

This does not mean every biblical sentence is false. The Quran confirms truth in earlier revelation, criticizes specific distortions, and judges disputed beliefs.

sections.title: The Christian Preservation Claim
sections.body:
Christians rightly point to passages saying that God's word endures, such as Isaiah 40:8 and Matthew 24:35. They often understand these promises to mean that God preserved the Bible's message despite copying differences. Christian scholars acknowledge manuscript variants but argue that the central message remains recoverable.

The Muslim question is not whether God can preserve revelation. It is whether these promises identify every later biblical book and reading as perfectly protected when manuscripts, canons, and Gospel accounts differ.

sections.title: Earlier Communities Were Entrusted With Revelation
sections.body:
Quran 5:44 says that prophets, rabbis, and scholars judged by the Torah because they were entrusted with God's Book. Entrustment is an honor and a test, but it leaves room for human failure.

The Quran accuses some people of writing a text and then claiming it came from God (2:79). It also criticizes twisted words, hidden truth, and forgotten reminders. These are specific charges, not a claim that no truth remains in earlier scripture.

sections.title: Jeremiah 8:8 and the Scribes
sections.body:
Jeremiah asks how people can claim to possess the law when 'the lying pen of the scribes has made it into a lie' (8:8). Some scholars understand this as falsifying written material. Others see deceptive interpretation by teachers who possessed the law but taught it falsely.

The verse should not prove more than it says. It does show the Bible criticizing authorities who turn written revelation into falsehood, whether through the pen, teaching, or both.

sections.title: The Quran Invites a Coherence Test
sections.body:
Quran 4:82 asks people to reflect on the Quran and says that a book from other than God would contain much contradiction. This does not label every difference a contradiction. It invites readers to examine a revelation's teaching about God, prophets, morality, and salvation.

For Muslims, the Quran's consistent monotheism is central evidence. It confirms earlier prophets while correcting doctrines that make a human messenger divine or transfer one person's guilt to another.

sections.title: A Distinct Promise for the Final Revelation
sections.body:
The Quran says, 'Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder. And indeed, We will be its guardian' (15:9). Muslims understand this promise as attached to the final revelation because no later prophet will restore it.

The verse need not stand alone as historical proof. Readers can compare it with early manuscripts, public recitation, memorization, the Uthmanic written tradition, and canonical readings. The theological promise and historical case support one another.

sections.title: What Tahrif Means
sections.body:
Tahrif means distortion. Muslim scholars use it for changing wording and for distorting a sound text through false interpretation, concealment, or selective quotation. Quran 2:79 supports some textual fabrication, while other passages criticize distortion in speech and meaning.

Classical scholars differed over its extent. The careful Islamic position is not that every verse in today's Bible was rewritten. It is that earlier revelation is no longer available as the final, fully reliable criterion. Truth remains, but it must be judged by the Quran.

sections.title: The Christian Response
sections.body:
Christian textual critics argue that many manuscripts help reconstruct early readings and that most variants are minor. They also note that no single doctrine rests only on one disputed word. These points matter.

They do not remove every difficulty. Some passages are absent from the earliest manuscripts. Christian traditions recognize different canons, and the Gospels sometimes give different accounts of the same event. A recoverable text still requires a decision about which books are revelation and which interpretation is true.

sections.title: Why God Allowed Human Failure
sections.body:
God allows people to misuse entrusted gifts such as knowledge, authority, wealth, and freedom without approving that misuse. Accountability would have little meaning if people could never betray a trust. Earlier scriptural corruption fits this pattern of moral testing.

Guidance was never extinguished. Prophets, faithful believers, and surviving truth continued to call people to God. The final revelation confirmed what was true, exposed distortions, and received a different promise of preservation.

sections.title: What Islam Does Not Claim
sections.body:
Islam does not require belief that the Bible contains no wisdom, history, or trace of revelation. It does not teach that variants make every document worthless. It also rejects invented manuscript claims and careless allegations.

The precise claim is this: the Torah and Gospel were true revelations. The present collection preserves some of that truth alongside human transmission and interpretation. The Quran is the final authority for distinguishing between them.

sections.title: The Bottom Line
sections.body: God's faithfulness does not require preventing every human abuse of revelation. In the Islamic account, He preserved guidance through successive prophets and finally through the Quran. The historical question is comparative: which scripture has the clearest preservation history, the most coherent message about God, and the strongest claim to be final? Islam directs that comparison toward the Quran.

sections.title: The Islamic Conclusion
sections.body: Scriptural distortion is not a failure of God's power. It shows human beings failing a trust while God continues to guide. The Bible still contains history, moral teaching, and traces of revelation. Its transmission and competing interpretations make a final criterion necessary. The Quran presents itself as that criterion: confirming the prophets, restoring monotheism, correcting disputed claims, and carrying a public promise of preservation.

quranVerses.translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by that with which they were entrusted of the Scripture of Allah, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers.

quranVerses.translation: So woe to those who write the "scripture" with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," in order to exchange it for a small price. Woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn.

faq.question: Does tahrif mean changed words or changed meaning?
faq.answer: Muslim scholars have used the term for both. Quran 2:79 supports at least some fabrication of wording, while other passages criticize concealment, selective quotation, and distorted interpretation. Islam does not require the claim that every biblical sentence was rewritten.

faq.question: Why was the Quran given a distinct preservation promise?
faq.answer: Earlier communities were followed by prophets who renewed guidance. The Quran presents itself as the final revelation, with no later prophet coming to restore it, and therefore as directly guarded by God (Quran 15:9).

faq.question: Is using Quran 15:9 circular?
faq.answer: The verse states the theological claim; it does not need to stand alone as historical proof. The claim can be compared with early manuscripts, mass recitation and memorization, the Uthmanic written tradition, and the controlled canonical readings.

faq.question: Do Christians claim that every Bible manuscript is identical?
faq.answer: No. Christian textual critics openly document variants and argue that the large manuscript tradition still allows most early readings and the central message to be recovered.

faq.question: Does Islam say the Bible contains no truth?
faq.answer: No. The Quran confirms genuine earlier revelation and the prophets it records. The Islamic claim is that surviving truth is mixed with human transmission and interpretation, making the Quran necessary as the final criterion.
